tracks.comment:
Chef’s Special (Off Menu)

Some records are made to fit neatly into a genre. This isn’t one of them.

Chef’s Special (Off Menu) is a 14-track collection of remixes, reinterpretations, and dance-floor experiments that travel through Afro house, Miami bass, Jersey club, tech house, baile funk, ghetto tech, juke, bass music, and everything in between.

The goal wasn’t to chase a trend or stay inside a lane. It was to ask a simple question: What happens when familiar songs are cooked differently?

Each track takes inspiration from a different corner of dance music culture while paying respect to the artists, cities, and communities that helped shape these sounds. Some moments are soulful. Some are high-energy. Some are built for the club at midnight. Others are meant for the ride home at 3 a.m.

This project is less of an album and more of a tasting menu. Fourteen courses. Fourteen different flavors. One kitchen.

Welcome to the Chef’s Special.

Not everything worth trying is on the menu.

Chef’s Special (Off Menu) is a 14-track collection of remixes, reinterpretations, and dance-floor experiments that travel through Afro house, Miami bass, Jersey club, tech house, baile funk, ghetto tech, juke, bass music, and everything in between.

The goal wasn’t to chase a trend or stay inside a lane. It was to ask a simple question: What happens when familiar songs are cooked differently?

Each track takes inspiration from a different corner of dance music culture while paying respect to the artists, cities, and communities that helped shape these sounds. Some moments are soulful. Some are high-energy. Some are built for the club at midnight. Others are meant for the ride home at 3 a.m.

This project is less of an album and more of a tasting menu. Fourteen courses. Fourteen different flavors. One kitchen.

Welcome to the Chef’s Special.

Not everything worth trying is on the menu.

tracks.comment:
HEADS KNOW has released its first-ever compilation album, US CLUB, on January 31st. Inspired by a tweet by Bok Bok that accidentally coined “US Club” — sparking rightful outrage from artists and veteran members of the club community — the platform wanted to use this project as a chance to not only educate others about club music’s true origins, but also as a chance to bring together producers from cities all over the states who’ve been helping keep club music alive today.

There’s no doubt that club music was created in Baltimore, taking direct inspiration from Ghetto House in Chicago. It spread to producers in places like Newark and Philadelphia, who added their own styles to the genre’s distinctive bounce. Now, the meaning of “club music” has morphed into almost any dancefloor-minded track made anywhere in the world. But US CLUB is an attempt to reclaim the roots of the genre while also showcasing its interpretations from various American cities.

We’re honored to feature tracks from one of Baltimore Club’s creators, DJ Technics, along with other pioneers, such as TRAXMAN and DJ Clent, who were instrumental in the evolution from ghetto house to footwork. It was also essential to have all of these tracks mastered by Nadus, a second-generation Jersey Club trailblazer who has supported HEADS KNOW since its inception.

“I handpicked all of the artists in this compilation,” HEADS KNOW founder Arielle Lana LeJarde says. “Not only did I aim to put the spotlight back on club music legends, but I also wanted to include artists who’ve made significant contributions to the scene throughout the years, plus some of my personal newer favorites.”

Other notable cuts come from DJ Problem, a member of the esteemed Brick Bandits collective, Dance Mania signee Dj Thadz, and Baltimore Club torchbearer CalvoMusic. The album also presents emerging club music mainstays bastiengoat, nextdimensional, HONEY B, Tromac, JEWELSSEA, and more.

US CLUB will be available on Bandcamp and SoundCloud. Part of its proceeds will be used to launch the HEADS KNOW Fund, which aims to distribute grants to: 1) Underground electronic music and hip-hop pioneers who are in urgent financial need of aid due to medical bills, natural disasters, or other emergencies. 2) Freelance culture journalists who need monetary assistance to complete an assignment. 3) Independent promoters that have either incurred a loss while throwing an event or will be hosting a party to raise funds for a charitable cause.
